cleanIntro: Henry's H014 book. The Long Ranger is the odd one out in the Henry lever range: a geared lever action feeding from a flush detachable box magazine, with no magazine tube anywhere on the gun. The magazine will not clear the lever unless the lever is closed — that catches people coming from the tube guns.

steps.title: Lever CLOSED before you reach for the magazine
steps.action: Counter-intuitive and worth getting right first: the lever must be closed, or near closed, to remove or insert the magazine. Open the lever fully and the magazine physically cannot clear it. Anyone used to opening the action first — which is the correct first move on every other Henry lever gun — will stand there wondering why the magazine is trapped.
steps.quote: NOTE: The lever should be closed or towards the closed/chambered position to remove or insert the magazine. The magazine will not clear the lever if the lever is all the way open.
steps.cite: Henry H014 Series User Manual — undated — no edition, revision or form code is printed in the book — HOW TO LOAD YOUR HENRY RIFLE, p.8

steps.title: Magazine released from the right side of the receiver
steps.action: With the lever closed, press the magazine release button on the RIGHT side of the receiver and pull down on the magazine. It is a flush-fit steel box, so there is little to grip — take hold of the floor plate rather than expecting it to drop free. There is a spring behind the release button so it will not let go on its own.
steps.prose: This rifle is equipped with a flush mount, all steel, detachable box magazine that holds cartridges in a staggered column.
steps.quote: To release the magazine push the magazine release button on the right side of the receiver and pull down on the magazine.
steps.cite: Henry H014 Series User Manual — undated — no edition, revision or form code is printed in the book — HOW TO LOAD YOUR HENRY RIFLE, p.8

steps.title: Magazine out first, THEN the lever opened to eject the chambered round
steps.action: Order matters here. Get the magazine out, and only then run the lever down to open the action and throw out whatever is in the chamber. Doing it the other way just chambers a fresh round from the magazine. Then look into the chamber and confirm it by eye — Henry asks for the double check in as many words.
steps.quote: To unload your Long Ranger, depress the magazine release button on the right hand side on the receiver and pull down on the magazine to remove it. Once the magazine is removed move the lever in a downward motion to open the action which will eject any live ammunition that is in the chamber. Be sure to double check the chamber to ensure the rifle is unloaded.
steps.cite: Henry H014 Series User Manual — undated — no edition, revision or form code is printed in the book — HOW TO UNLOAD YOUR HENRY LONG RANGER RIFLE, p.9

steps.title: Transfer bar, and what it means for carrying
steps.action: The Long Ranger uses the patented transfer-bar safety: it fires only with the hammer fully cocked and the trigger pulled, and it is designed to be carried with the hammer fully down. There is no half-cock and no crossbolt on this rifle, so a partially lowered hammer is not a safe condition, it is just a hammer that has not been put down properly.
steps.quote: This firearm is designed with an ultra-safe patented Transfer Bar Safety Mechanism.
steps.cite: Henry H014 Series User Manual — undated — no edition, revision or form code is printed in the book — TRANSFER BAR SAFETY, p.8

steps.title: Action open, ammunition out of the cleaning area
steps.action: Open the action, confirm the rifle is completely unloaded, and keep the muzzle pointed somewhere safe for the duration. Move the ammunition away before the solvent comes out. Henry also wants the chambers cleaned promptly after shooting rather than left — brass left standing in a chamber sweats moisture onto it.
steps.aside: NOTICE! It is very important that the chambers of your rifle be cleaned thoroughly and promptly after shooting.
steps.quote: OPEN THE ACTION AND MAKE CERTAIN YOUR FIREARM IS COMPLETELY UNLOADED. KEEP THE MUZZLE POINTED IN A SAFE DIRECTION.
steps.cite: Henry H014 Series User Manual — undated — no edition, revision or form code is printed in the book — CLEANING SAFETY PRECAUTIONS, p.11

steps.title: Lever cycled forward, bore cleaned breech to muzzle
steps.action: Cycle the lever forward to open the action and run the rod down the bore from the breech toward the muzzle. That is the whole mechanical preparation — the Long Ranger is cleaned assembled. Inspect the chamber and bore first: with .223, .243, .308 and 6.5 Creedmoor in the range, jacketed bullets at rifle velocity leave copper as well as powder.
steps.quote: In order to clean it, we suggest that you first open the action by cycling the lever forward. Inspect the chamber and bore for brass, copper and powder fouling. Using a brand name cleaning kit, run the cleaning rod down the bore from the breech towards the muzzle.
steps.cite: Henry H014 Series User Manual — undated — no edition, revision or form code is printed in the book — HOW TO CLEAN YOUR HENRY RIFLE, p.12

steps.title: Always in the direction the bullet went
steps.action: Follow the bullet, every time. Henry's reasoning is that the fouling is in the barrel while the chamber and receiver are clean, so a brush or patch driven in from the muzzle pushes dirt and moisture into the chamber and receiver — and that is a leading cause of stuck cases. On a rifle cartridge with a bottleneck case, a gritty chamber is a real extraction problem.
steps.quote: ALWAYS CLEAN FROM THE NATURAL DIRECTION OF THE BULLET.
steps.cite: Henry H014 Series User Manual — undated — no edition, revision or form code is printed in the book — HOW TO CLEAN YOUR HENRY RIFLE, p.12
steps.warn: If you run a brush or patch from the muzzle end you will push this dirt, residue, and moisture into the chamber and receiver. This is a major cause of stuck cases or problems.

steps.title: Clean patch surface each pass, brush never reversed
steps.action: Turn up a clean face of patch for every trip down the barrel. A used surface carries the abrasive dirt from the muzzle back into the chamber and neck, and the next bullet drags it through the throat — Henry calls that the exact equivalent of cleaning in the wrong direction. Never reverse a brush inside the bore either; it folds the bristles and finishes the brush.
steps.aside: NEVER GO BACK AND FORTH REVERSING THE BRUSH.
steps.quote: USE A CLEAN PATCH SURFACE EACH TIME YOU GO DOWN THE BARREL.
steps.cite: Henry H014 Series User Manual — undated — no edition, revision or form code is printed in the book — HOW TO CLEAN YOUR HENRY RIFLE, p.12

steps.title: Rod kept off the bore, especially at the crown
steps.action: Keep the rod and its tip centred so neither rubs the bore. On an accuracy rifle this is not fussiness — rod marks and a damaged crown are permanent and they show up on target. Henry notes that an experienced eye can read a barrel's cleaning history off the inside of it, which is a polite way of saying the damage is obvious and self-inflicted.
steps.quote: CENTER THE TOP AND ROD. BE CAREFUL NOT TO LET EITHER RUB THE BORE.
steps.cite: Henry H014 Series User Manual — undated — no edition, revision or form code is printed in the book — HOW TO CLEAN YOUR HENRY RIFLE, p.12

steps.title: Bolt wiped and oiled
steps.action: Wipe the bolt clean of debris with solvent on a patch or small rag and then oil it. Reach the bolt face and the extractor hook — a bottleneck rifle case leaves carbon under the hook, and a fouled extractor on a rifle-calibre lever gun shows up as a case left in the chamber. Keep the oil light so it does not run into the lockwork.
steps.quote: Wipe the bolt clean of any debris with solvent and a patch or small rag. Spray the bolt with some gun oil.
steps.cite: Henry H014 Series User Manual — undated — no edition, revision or form code is printed in the book — HOW TO CLEAN YOUR HENRY RIFLE, p.13

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: That is Henry's published routine for the Long Ranger, done with the rifle assembled. The manual states the rifle does not need disassembly to be cleaned properly and publishes no takedown procedure of any kind, so there is no Deep Clean branch — there is nothing further Henry documents for the owner to do.
steps.quote: You do not have to disassemble this rifle in order to clean it sufficiently and to keep it operating properly.
steps.cite: Henry H014 Series User Manual — undated — no edition, revision or form code is printed in the book — HOW TO CLEAN YOUR HENRY RIFLE, p.12

deepAbsentReason: Henry's H014 book publishes no disassembly procedure. Printed p.12 states 'You do not have to disassemble this rifle in order to clean it sufficiently and to keep it operating properly.' and 'NOTICE! DO NOT ATTEMPT TO TAKE YOUR FIREARM APART FURTHER THAN EXPLAINED IN THIS MANUAL.', and nothing further than the bore, bolt and magazine is explained anywhere in the 17 printed pages. The only component-level procedures in the book are scope-mount installation (p.9), sight adjustment (p.10) and hammer-extension fitting (p.10), none of which is disassembly for cleaning. ⛔ The receiver-cover teardown printed in the H001 and H004 rimfire books was NOT carried across: the Long Ranger is a different action entirely — a geared lever action with a rotating bolt head and a detachable box magazine, on an aerospace alloy receiver — and it has no inner magazine tube and no receiver cover of that pattern. Likewise the H009 .30/30 book's lever-screw-and-bolt takedown belongs to that rifle, not to this one. No deep procedure exists to author.

cleaning.name: BORE & CHAMBER
tasks: Run a solvent-wet patch from the breech toward the muzzle, following the bullet
Fresh patch surface every pass; work at copper fouling until patches come out clean
Dry the bore, lightly oil, and wipe the chamber and its neck area

cleaning.name: BOLT & ACTION
tasks: Wipe the bolt face and clean carbon from under the extractor hook, then oil lightly
Wipe the reachable receiver interior with the lever open
Keep solvent out of the trigger mechanism — it drains down and leaves the trigger gummy

cleaning.name: MAGAZINE & EXTERIOR
tasks: Wipe the steel magazine body and follower dry; check the feed lips are undamaged
Wipe the magazine well and the release button surround
Film of oil on exposed steel; wipe the checkered walnut with a dry cloth

reassembly: Close the lever fully before offering the magazine back up — it will not clear an open lever.
Insert the magazine into the receiver until it clicks into place, then pull down on it to confirm it is locked.
Cycle the lever to confirm the action runs smoothly through full travel.
Lower the hammer fully down; this rifle has no half-cock, so fully down is the carry position.
fncheck: With the rifle confirmed empty, close the lever and confirm an empty magazine seats with a click and is retained when pulled down on, cycle the lever through full travel and confirm it closes fully home, and confirm the hammer falls only from full cock with the trigger pulled.
